parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and is the case split the rest of §4–§7 rests on. As literally stated the dichotomy is false: f(x)=x+1 satisfies (1) (QM-AM-GM, as the text's own Verification shows), has V={1} with at most one positive value, yet g is not identically 0 and branch (ii) fails since it demands 'both values attainable'. This particular omission is nearly self-repairing (V={c} is exactly the target conclusion, and §7 states g≡c). The second half of the witness is a real gap: the dichotomy presupposes g≥0, but the text only records g(x)>-x and §3 rules out two distinct POSITIVE values; nowhere is a negative value of g excluded (the easy orbit argument x+ng(x)>0 from (4) is never written). Hence necessity as written does not cover all cases.
